newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Syfrets fund manager sees rand at 4.70 at end 1997.
newsitem.headline: Syfrets fund manager sees rand at 4.70 at end 1997.

text.p: South African investment manager Syfrets expects the rand to stabilise as the balance of payments improves in 1997, with the currency ending 1997 at 4.70 to the dollar -- unchanged from present levels.

In a quarterly economic review, economist Sandra Gordon said consumer spending was likely to slow sharply in the face of high interest rates and record levels of household debt, while exports would get a boost from the weaker rand.
"The net result of the anticipated reduction in the trade imbalance, coupled with limited capital inflows, is that the funds outflow will diminish and then finally reverse," she said.
"This will provide fundamental support for the rand, which is expected to stabilise around current levels during the year ahead. A rand/dollar exchange of 4.70 is forecast at the end of 1997."

Gordon said the latest fall in the rand and the evaporation of foreign investment had forced up short-term interest rates and delayed any reduction in interest rates until the second quarter of 1997 at the earliest.
But she predicted the Reserve Bank would still be in a position to announce interest rate cuts twice next year.

That rate relief, coupled with a strengthening world economy, should help the South African economy recover in 1998 after an expected slowdown in growth to under 2.5 percent in 1997 from 3.0 percent this year and 3.3 percent in 1995.
